description:
Found by the HexDocs cold test (defk-djy.9, docs/cold-tests/hexdocs-entropy.md, error 2 and point 6). for w <- 0..(n - 1) do ... end used as a value is rejected with for-collect and the hint 'allocate the output array and write it in the loop', with no rewrite, while most first-write errors give one (unknown-function, pipe, Enum.sum). The tester needed the catalogue page for the shape out = alloc(f64, n); for i <- ... do out[i] = ... end; out.

Done when a for without reduce: used as a value, over a range i <- 0..(n - 1)//1 or an array x <- a with a simple body, gets a rewrite built from the author's code (alloc of the length, a for writing out[i] = <body value>, then out; the element type from the body's type where the compiler knows it, else a placeholder the hint names), the rewrite compiles where it is shown (test in compile_errors_test 'targeted hints'), and the catalogue entry is unchanged or regenerated.
title: for-collect: a rewrite from the author's own loop (alloc the output, write out[i])
